vault.owner_connects: Only an owner can connect the Family Document Vault.

vault.step_paste: Paste the key's connection string here, and its client secret if you didn't include it in the string.

switch.accounts_hint: Each account in the export becomes a new Montra account, goes into one you already have, or is left out.
switch.actual.note: Actual’s full backup (Settings, Export data) is a database file Montra can’t read: export the transactions CSV instead.
switch.actual.step_1: In Actual, open an account (or All accounts) and use the account menu’s Export option to save a CSV.
switch.actual.step_2: Upload the CSV. Split transactions come in as their parts.
switch.balance_today_hint: Owed, for cards and loans. The opening balance is worked out so this is where it ends up.
switch.bank.note: Banks keep a limited history online, often 90 days to a few years. Each file’s closing balance sets its account’s balance here.
switch.bank.step_1: Sign in to your bank’s website and open an account’s transactions. Look for Download or Export.
switch.bank.step_2: Choose OFX, QFX (Quicken) or Microsoft Money as the format, and the longest date range the bank allows.
switch.bank.step_3: Do the same for each account and bank, then upload all the files together: each account in them becomes its own.
switch.batch_counts: {added} added · {matched} matched with what was already there
switch.categories_hint: Rows keep their category from the export. Transfers and card payments are best left out: they’re paired as transfers after the import.
switch.check_signs: Exports differ in how they show spending. On the next screen, check money in and out for each account: if spending shows up as money in, tick “Spending shows as positive” for that file.
switch.copilot.step_1: On iPhone: Settings, scroll to Account, then Export your transactions, and save or share the file. On Mac, iPad or the web: filter the Transactions list and export it.
switch.empower.note: Empower exports what’s on screen, and no investment holdings: bring those over as account balances.
switch.empower.step_1: Open Empower’s Personal Dashboard in a web browser.
switch.empower.step_2: Go to Overview, then Transactions, and choose all accounts and the date range you want.
switch.empower.step_3: Click CSV next to “Search transactions”, then upload the file.
switch.goodbudget.step_1: In Goodbudget, open the account and click Export CSV above its transactions.
switch.goodbudget.step_2: Do the same for each account, then upload all the files together. Envelopes come over as categories.
switch.inverted: Spending shows as positive in this file
switch.lunch_money.step_1: Open Lunch Money in a web browser and go to Transactions.
switch.lunch_money.step_2: Clear any filters and set the date range you want to bring over: the export has exactly what’s on screen.
switch.lunch_money.step_3: Click the Export to CSV icon at the right, above the table, and upload the file.
switch.mint.step_1: Mint closed in March 2024. If you kept the transactions.csv you exported from it, upload that.
switch.mint.step_2: Without it, download statements from your banks instead (most offer CSV) and choose “Another app or spreadsheet”.
switch.monarch.note: Monarch downloads at most 10,000 transactions at a time. With more, download a few date ranges and upload them together.
switch.monarch.step_1: Open Monarch in a web browser.
switch.monarch.step_2: Go to Settings, then Data, and choose Download transactions. (Or open an account, click Edit, then Download transactions, for one account at a time.)
switch.monarch.step_3: Upload the CSV file it downloads.
switch.new_workspace: Start a new workspace for the import
switch.next_steps: Next: review anything Montra wasn’t sure about, and set up a budget.
switch.not_fresh: {count, plural, one {This workspace has # transaction of its own.} other {This workspace has # transactions of its own.}} Switching works on a fresh start, so nothing has to be merged with what’s here and nothing is lost.
switch.nothing_to_import: Choose at least one account to import.
switch.opening_owed_from_file: Owed at the start of the export: {amount}
switch.other.step_1: Export your transactions as CSV or Excel: dates, descriptions and amounts, ideally with an Account and a Category column.
switch.other.step_2: Upload the files. With an Account column, each account becomes its own import; without one, each file is one account.
switch.pick: Which app are you coming from?
switch.plan_hint: Nothing is created until you start the import. Each account becomes its own import, so you can check every one before it goes in.
switch.pocketsmith.step_1: In PocketSmith, go to Transactions, then All transactions.
switch.pocketsmith.step_2: Hover over Export, choose CSV, and upload the file.
switch.preparing: Preparing a preview of each account…
switch.problem_needs_mapping: Its columns aren’t clear: import it on the Import page, where you can map them.
switch.problem_no_transactions: No transactions found in this file.
switch.problem_unsupported_type: Not a CSV, Excel, QIF or OFX file: import it on the Import page instead.
switch.quicken_mac.note: Quicken for Mac can’t export QIF, so export each register as CSV. Moving from Quicken for Windows? Choose Quicken (Windows) instead.
switch.quicken_mac.step_1: In Quicken for Mac, open an account’s register, then File, Export, Register Transactions to CSV File, with All visible.
switch.quicken_mac.step_2: Do the same for each account and upload all the files together (each file is one account).
switch.quicken_windows.note: Investment accounts are left out (Montra doesn’t import buys, sells or dividends yet). Quicken writes two-digit years and your Windows date order: check the dates on the next screen.
switch.quicken_windows.step_1: In Quicken, choose File, then File Export, then QIF File.
switch.quicken_windows.step_2: Pick one account under Quicken Account to Export From, set the dates to include everything, tick Transactions, and save the file.
switch.quicken_windows.step_3: Do the same for each account, then upload all the files together (each file is one account). Transfers between them are paired.
switch.ready: Every account has its preview. Check any of them, then import them all.
switch.rocket_money.step_1: In Rocket Money, go to Transactions and choose Export (on the web) or the menu, then CSV Download (in the app).
switch.rocket_money.step_2: Pick the accounts and dates, then Export. Rocket Money emails you a download link: open it on a computer.
switch.simplifi.note: To bring split transactions over as their parts, turn on Show split transactions (the gear icon) before exporting.
switch.simplifi.step_1: Open Quicken Simplifi in a web browser (the app can’t export).
switch.simplifi.step_2: Go to Transactions. Use Filter, then Account, to tick all your accounts, and set a custom date range if you need one.
switch.simplifi.step_3: Open the three-dot menu next to Filter, choose Export to CSV, and upload the file.
switch.statements_instead: To add a bank or card statement to this workspace, use Import instead.
switch.subtitle: Move your accounts, transactions and categories into Montra in one go.
switch.tiller.step_1: Open your Tiller spreadsheet and go to the Transactions sheet.
switch.tiller.step_2: In Google Sheets choose File, Download, Comma-separated values (.csv); in Excel save the sheet as CSV. Upload that file.

switch.ynab.note: Each account’s Starting Balance becomes its opening balance, and transfers between your YNAB accounts are paired as transfers.
switch.ynab.step_1: Open YNAB in a web browser (the phone apps can’t export).
switch.ynab.step_2: Click your plan’s name at the top left, then Export Plan.
switch.ynab.step_3: YNAB downloads your plan and your transactions. Upload the transactions file (its name ends in “Register”); unzip it first if it came as a zip.
